name: @argszero/dsh-git-hook-guard
description: The harness runs its own git commands — working-tree snapshots at turn start, tree diffs, ignore checks — and a git command reads the working directory's repository configuration. `GitRunner.run()` scrubs the environment (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0, the credential scrub) but passes no -c flags, so a .git/config that a clone brought along still decides where hooks live: with `core.hooksPath .hooks` and a repository-shipped `.hooks/post-index-change`, `git add --all --ignore-errors` executes that file with the DSH user's privileges at turn start, with no tool call requested (reported as #9382; the `core.fsmonitor` half is #9217). This plugin shadows `spawn` on the subprocess service instance and, for git invocations the harness itself starts, inserts the two flags the repository's own code already uses (`packages/experimental/worktree/src/index.ts`): `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false`. The default scope is the harness's own bookkeeping calls — an invocation whose environment carries the GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 credential-scrub marker — so a git command the user asks for through the shell (argv[0] is the shell) is untouched, and a caller that sets its own git config is respected rather than overridden. Zero runtime dependencies, fail-open, no sandbox changes.
